content: To ensure maximum contraceptive effectiveness, Alesse® (levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol tablets) must be taken exactly as directed, without exceeding intervals of 24 hours between doses. The prescribed regimen involves taking one pink tablet daily for 21 consecutive days, followed by one light-green inert tablet daily for 7 consecutive days. It is recommended to take the tablets at the same time each day. The pill dispenser should be stored in the wallet provided to prevent fading of the pills. If the pills fade, they should still be taken as directed. First Cycle of Use Before starting Alesse, the possibility of ovulation and conception prior to initiation should be considered. Patients should begin taking Alesse either on the first Sunday after the onset of menstruation (Sunday Start) or on the first day of menstruation (Day 1 Start). Sunday Start Patients should begin Alesse-28 on the first Sunday after menstruation begins. If menstruation starts on a Sunday, the first pink tablet should be taken that day. One pink tablet is taken daily for 21 consecutive days, followed by one light-green inert tablet daily for 7 consecutive days. Withdrawal bleeding typically occurs within 3 days after stopping the pink tablets and may not be complete before starting the next pack. During the first cycle, Alesse-28 should not be relied upon for contraception until a pink tablet has been taken daily for 7 consecutive days. A nonhormonal backup method of birth control should be used during these 7 days. Day 1 Start Patients should begin taking Alesse-28 within the first 24 hours of their period (Day 1 of the menstrual cycle). One pink tablet is taken daily for 21 consecutive days, followed by one light-green inert tablet daily for 7 consecutive days. Withdrawal bleeding typically occurs within 3 days after stopping the pink tablets and may not be complete before starting the next pack. If Alesse is started on Day 1 of the menstrual cycle, no backup contraception is necessary. If Alesse-28 is started later than Day 1 of the first menstrual cycle or postpartum, a nonhormonal backup method of birth control should be used for the first 7 consecutive days of administration. After the First Cycle The next and all subsequent courses of Alesse should begin the day after the last light-green tablet is taken. The same dosing schedule should be followed: 21 days of pink tablets followed by 7 days of light-green tablets. If the patient starts a new pack later than the proper day, a nonhormonal backup method of birth control should be used until a pink tablet has been taken daily for 7 consecutive days. Switching from Another Hormonal Contraceptive From a 21-day regimen: Wait 7 days after the last tablet before starting Alesse. Withdrawal bleeding will likely occur during this week. Ensure no more than 7 days pass after the previous regimen. From a 28-day regimen: Start Alesse the day after the last tablet of the previous pack. Do not wait any days between packs. From a progestin-only pill: Start Alesse the next day. From an implant or injection: Start Alesse on the day of implant removal or the day the next injection would be due. In all cases, use a nonhormonal backup method of birth control for the first 7 days of Alesse administration. Spotting or Breakthrough Bleeding If spotting or breakthrough bleeding occurs, the patient should continue taking the tablets as directed. This type of bleeding is usually transient and not clinically significant. However, if the bleeding persists or becomes prolonged, the patient should consult their physician. Risk of Pregnancy if Tablets Are Missed The likelihood of ovulation increases with each successive day that scheduled pink tablets are missed. If withdrawal bleeding does not occur, pregnancy should be considered. If the patient has not adhered to the prescribed schedule (e.g., missed one or more tablets or started late), pregnancy should be evaluated at the time of the first missed period. If the patient has adhered to the regimen but misses two consecutive periods, pregnancy should be ruled out. The risk of pregnancy increases with each missed active (pink) tablet. Use After Pregnancy, Abortion, or Miscarriage Postpartum (non-lactating) or after a second-trimester abortion: Alesse may be initiated no earlier than Day 28 due to the increased risk of thromboembolism. A nonhormonal backup method should be used for the first 7 days of tablet-taking. After a first-trimester abortion or miscarriage: Alesse may be started immediately. If started immediately, no backup contraception is needed. What to Do If You Miss Pills Miss 1 pink active pill: Take it as soon as you remember. Take the next pill at your regular time, even if it means taking two pills in one day. Use a nonhormonal backup method (e.g., condoms or spermicide) for the next 7 days if you have sex. Miss 2 pink active pills in a row in Week 1 or Week 2: Take 2 pills on the day you remember and 2 pills the next day. Then take 1 pill daily until the pack is finished. Use a nonhormonal backup method for the next 7 days if you have sex. Miss 2 pink active pills in a row in Week 3: Day 1 Starter: Discard the rest of the pack and start a new pack the same day. Sunday Starter: Continue taking 1 pill daily until Sunday. On Sunday, discard the rest of the pack and start a new pack. You may not have a period this month, but this is expected. If you miss your period for two consecutive months, contact your healthcare provider as you may be pregnant. Use a nonhormonal backup method for the next 7 days if you have sex. Miss 3 or more pink active pills in a row (during the first 3 weeks): Day 1 Starter: Discard the rest of the pack and start a new pack the same day. Sunday Starter: Continue taking 1 pill daily until Sunday. On Sunday, discard the rest of the pack and start a new pack. You may not have a period this month, but this is expected. If you miss your period for two consecutive months, contact your healthcare provider as you may be pregnant. Use a nonhormonal backup method for the next 7 days if you have sex. Miss any of the 7 light-green reminder pills in Week 4: Discard the missed pills. Continue taking 1 pill daily until the pack is empty. No backup contraception is needed if you start your next pack on time.
